newsitem.title: USA: US lawmaker opposes access charges for Internet.
newsitem.headline: US lawmaker opposes access charges for Internet.

text.p: The head of the Senate Commerce Commitee said Friday he opposes proposals that would require the Federal Communications Commission to levy charges on firms that provide access to the Internet.

The FCC, as part of its proposal to reform the complex set of charges that long-distance carriers pay to hook up to local phone networks, has itself tentatively concluded against imposing such fees on Internet service providers.
Local carriers, citing congestion on their networks from Internet traffic, had asked the FCC to do so.
"The cure for telephone network congestion isn't putting more toll booths on the Information Superhighway," Sen John McCain, an Arizona Republican, said in a statement.

"The solution is to provide incentives to telephone companies to install new data-friendly digital switches that will not only alleviate congestion but also provide PC users with much higher-speed access to the Internet."
